title: Dialog
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) for a message; sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:) for content
summary: A modal is the system alert for a short message and the system sheet for content. Inside a Monarch theme the sheet's content uses Monarch components and colours. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Use alert to tell the person something or ask a short question. Use sheet for a focused task with its own controls: a form, a picker, details. Put Cancel and the confirming action in the sheet's toolbar.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a centred dialog box over a dimmed screen yourself. For a short bottom panel see drawer; for a destructive confirmation see confirm-dialog.
api: func alert(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View

states.name: alert
states.description: Centred over a dimmed screen, with a title, a message and up to a few buttons.

states.name: sheet
states.description: A card that covers most of the screen on iPhone and is a centred form sheet on iPad.

states.name: dismissal blocked
states.description: With interactiveDismissDisabled the sheet does not close on a swipe; a button must close it.

appearance: The system draws the alert and the sheet's card, corners and dimming. The sheet's content is the app's: give it a theme background such as bgCanvas and it follows the four themes, because a sheet inherits the environment of the view that presents it, including the Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web Dialog is one component with sizes, a footer, a close button with closeLabel, busy, closeOnOutsideClick, escapeGuard and fullScreenOnPhone. On iOS the size is the system's (presentationDetents changes a sheet's height, see drawer), the footer is the navigation toolbar of a NavigationStack inside the sheet, the close button is a toolbar button, escapeGuard is interactiveDismissDisabled, and fullScreenOnPhone is fullScreenCover. Focus trapping and focus return are the system's (see focus-trap). Android uses a Material Dialog or a full-screen dialog.
accessibility: System behaviour: alerts and sheets are modal; VoiceOver, Switch Control and the keyboard are confined to them.
System behaviour: focus returns to the presenting screen on dismissal.
System behaviour: the escape gesture dismisses a sheet and chooses Cancel in an alert.
Give a sheet a navigation title so it is announced, and a visible button that closes it.
edgeCases: A sheet presented from a sheet stacks; avoid more than two levels.
State changed in a sheet is not saved by dismissal; apply it in the confirming action or in onDismiss.
Alerts cannot contain custom views other than text fields and buttons.
